fullPassage: The "sharing economy" is a system based on the idea of individuals renting things from each other through the internet. Things now commonly rented in this way include houses, cars, boats, and power tools. These items are considered by many to be too expensive to own but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price. This collaborative use of resources has several positive effects. Owners make money from the things they own, and renters pay less than they would if they bought the things themselves or rented them from a company such as a car rental agency. The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than buying the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products. As more people use sharing services, these benefits are likely to grow.

questions.passage: The "sharing economy" is a system based on the idea of individuals renting things from each other through the internet. These items are considered by many to be too (A)[cheap / expensive] to own but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price. Owners make money from the things they own, and renters pay less than they would if they bought the things themselves or rented them from a company such as a car rental agency. The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than buying the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) expensive=비싼 / cheap=싼 (B) positive=긍정적인 / negative=부정적인 (C) grow=증가하다 / shrink=줄어들다
det.analysis:
① expensive—positive—grow: 물건이 너무 비싸(expensive) 소유하기 부담되고, 자원 공유는 긍정적(positive) 효과가 있으며, 더 많은 사람이 이용할수록 이익이 증가한다(grow) ←정답
② cheap/shrink: 싸다·줄어든다는 문맥과 반대
③ negative: 부정적 효과가 아니라 긍정적 효과
④ cheap/negative: 싸다·부정적 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 물건이 비싸서(expensive) 공유하고, 공유의 긍정적(positive) 효과가 커진다(grow)는 흐름

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) individuals=개인들 / companies=회사들 (B) collaborative=협력적인 / competitive=경쟁적인 (C) benefits=이익을 얻다 / suffers=해를 입다
det.analysis:
① companies: 서로 빌리는 주체는 회사가 아니라 개인들(individuals)
② competitive/suffers: 경쟁적·해를 입다는 문맥과 반대
③ individuals—collaborative—benefits: 개인들이 인터넷으로 서로 빌리고, 자원의 협력적(collaborative) 사용이며, 환경도 이익을 얻는다(benefits) ←정답
④ companies—competitive—suffers: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 개인들(individuals)의 협력적(collaborative) 공유로 환경이 이익을 얻는다(benefits)는 흐름

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) willing=기꺼이 ~하는 / reluctant=꺼리는 (B) less=더 적게 / more=더 많이 (C) fewer=더 적은 / more=더 많은
det.analysis:
① reluctant: 물건 주인은 공유를 꺼리는(reluctant) 것이 아니라 기꺼이(willing) 공유함
② willing—less—fewer: 주인은 기꺼이(willing) 공유하고, 빌리는 사람은 더 적게(less) 내며, 자원도 더 적게(fewer) 소비된다 ←정답
③ more/more: 더 많이 낸다·더 많은 자원 소비는 공유의 이점과 반대
④ reluctant/more: 꺼리다·더 많이는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 기꺼이(willing) 공유 → 비용을 덜(less) 내고 자원을 덜(fewer) 쓴다는 이점의 흐름

④ rent: 소유하지 않고 일정 기간 사용하려고 돈을 내다 → 빌리다 ←정답
det.tip: pay money + use for a period + without owning → rent(빌리다)

questions.passage: These items are __________ (consider) by many to be too expensive to own but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: consider(동사: 여기다) → considered(과거분사). be동사 뒤 수동태 be + p.p. 구문
det.analysis: consider를 과거분사 considered로 변환. 'These items are considered by many'는 'be + 과거분사 + by' 수동태로 '~에 의해 여겨진다'는 의미. 주어(items)가 여겨지는 대상이므로 수동형이 필요
det.tip: are ____ by many → 수동태(be + p.p.) → considered

questions.passage: The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than __________ (buy) the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: buy(동사: 사다) → buying(동명사). rather than 뒤 병렬 구조의 동명사
det.analysis: buy를 동명사 buying으로 변환. 'sharing a product ... rather than buying the product'에서 rather than은 앞의 sharing과 병렬을 이루어 동일한 형태(동명사)를 요구하므로 buying이 필요
det.tip: sharing ... rather than ____ → 병렬 구조 → 동명사 buying

questions.passage: The "sharing economy" is a system based on the idea of individuals renting things from each other through the internet. Things now commonly rented in this way include houses, cars, boats, and power tools. These items are considered by many to be too expensive to own but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price. This collaborative use of resources has several __________. Owners make money from the things they own, and renters pay less than they would if they bought the things themselves or rented them from a company such as a car rental agency. The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than buying the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products. As more people use sharing services, these benefits are likely to grow.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: negative results=부정적 결과 / positive effects=긍정적 효과 / hidden costs=숨은 비용 / minor problems=사소한 문제
det.analysis:
① negative results: 뒤 문장들이 이점(돈 벌기·비용 절감·환경 보호)을 나열하므로 부정적이지 않음
② positive effects: 자원의 협력적 사용이 여러 긍정적 효과를 가지며, 뒤에 구체적 이점이 이어진다 ←정답
③ hidden costs: 숨은 비용? 뒤 문맥과 반대
④ minor problems: 사소한 문제? 이점 나열과 안 맞음
det.tip: 뒤에 이어지는 이점 나열(돈·비용 절감·환경) → several positive effects

questions.passage: The "sharing economy" is a system based on the idea of individuals renting things from each other through the internet. Things now commonly rented in this way include houses, cars, boats, and power tools. These items are considered by many to be __________ but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price. This collaborative use of resources has several positive effects. Owners make money from the things they own, and renters pay less than they would if they bought the things themselves or rented them from a company such as a car rental agency. The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than buying the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products. As more people use sharing services, these benefits are likely to grow.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: too expensive to own=소유하기엔 너무 비싼 / cheap enough to buy=살 만큼 싼 / easy to replace=교체하기 쉬운 / difficult to find=찾기 어려운
det.analysis:
① too expensive to own: 소유하기엔 너무 비싸지만 남이 소유해 값을 받고 공유한다는 뒤 문맥과 연결 ←정답
② cheap enough to buy: 살 만큼 싸다? 공유하는 이유(비쌈)와 반대
③ easy to replace: 교체하기 쉬운? 문맥 부적절
④ difficult to find: 찾기 어려운? 값·소유 이야기와 안 맞음
det.tip: but are owned by others who share them for a price(값을 받고 공유) → 비싸서(too expensive to own) 공유
